questions.question: Which holiday is celebrated on 31 October?
questions.fact: Halloween comes from "All Hallows' Eve", the night before All Saints' Day, mixed with the old Celtic festival of Samhain.

questions.question: In which country is Thanksgiving held on the fourth Thursday of November?
questions.fact: The first Thanksgiving is usually traced to a 1621 harvest feast between English settlers and the Wampanoag people.

questions.question: What is traditionally carved for Halloween?
questions.fact: Before pumpkins, people in Ireland and Scotland carved turnips to scare away evil spirits.

questions.question: Which Hindu festival is the "festival of lights"?
questions.fact: During Diwali, homes are lit with small oil lamps called diyas to celebrate light winning over darkness.

questions.question: Holi is known as the festival of…
questions.fact: During Holi, people throw coloured powder and water at each other to welcome spring.

questions.question: Hanukkah candles are lit on a…
questions.fact: The Hanukkah menorah has nine branches: eight for the nights of the festival, plus one used to light the others.

questions.question: When is Ramadan?
options: It moves each year with the lunar calendar
questions.fact: The Islamic calendar is about 11 days shorter than ours, so Ramadan comes earlier each year.

questions.question: What is Chinese New Year also called?
questions.fact: Chinese New Year falls between late January and mid-February and causes the largest yearly human migration on Earth.

questions.question: How many animals are in the Chinese zodiac?
questions.fact: The 12 animals are rat, ox, tiger, rabbit, dragon, snake, horse, goat, monkey, rooster, dog and pig.

questions.question: Which of these animals is not in the Chinese zodiac?
questions.fact: Legend says the cat missed the race to join the zodiac because the rat didn't wake it up. Vietnam's zodiac has a cat instead of the rabbit.

questions.question: What is traditionally given in red envelopes at Chinese New Year?
questions.fact: Red stands for luck and happiness in Chinese culture. Today many red envelopes are sent digitally by phone.

questions.question: When is Mexico's Day of the Dead mainly celebrated?
questions.fact: Families build altars called "ofrendas" with photos, candles, marigolds and the favourite food of loved ones who have died.

questions.question: Cinco de Mayo remembers a battle won by which country?
questions.fact: Cinco de Mayo remembers Mexico's victory over French troops at Puebla in 1862. It's often bigger in the US than in Mexico.

questions.question: In which country did the Christmas tree tradition first become popular?
questions.fact: Queen Victoria's German husband, Prince Albert, helped make Christmas trees popular in Britain in the 1840s.

questions.question: What is Saint Nicholas called in the Netherlands?
questions.fact: Sinterklaas arrives in the Netherlands by steamboat "from Spain" each November.

questions.question: In Catalonia, which Christmas log is hit with sticks until it "poops" presents?
questions.fact: Caga Tió is a log with a smiley face and a red hat. Children "feed" it for weeks before Christmas.

questions.question: Which traditional charcoal-burner brings Christmas presents in the Basque Country?
questions.fact: Olentzero comes down from the mountains on Christmas Eve, usually shown with a pipe and a beret.

questions.question: In Italy, which kind witch brings gifts on 6 January?
questions.fact: La Befana rides a broom and leaves sweets for good children and coal for naughty ones.

questions.question: Who is Krampus in Alpine folklore?
options: A horned creature who punishes naughty children
questions.fact: On Krampusnacht, 5 December, people in Austria and Bavaria dress up as Krampus and roam the streets.

questions.question: Which saint's day in Catalonia, 23 April, is celebrated with books and roses?
questions.fact: Sant Jordi is Saint George, the patron saint of Catalonia, who in the legend slew a dragon to save a princess.

questions.question: What do people give each other in Catalonia on Sant Jordi?
questions.fact: Millions of roses and over a million books are sold in Catalonia on Sant Jordi.

questions.question: Which night in June is celebrated with bonfires and fireworks in Spain?
questions.fact: On the night of San Juan, people jump over bonfires and some go into the sea at midnight for good luck.

questions.question: What is Barcelona's big city festival in September called?
questions.fact: La Mercè features giants, human towers and the "correfoc", where devils run through the streets with fireworks.

questions.question: What are the Semana Santa processions in Spain for?
questions.fact: Seville and Málaga have some of Spain's most famous Semana Santa processions, with huge floats called "pasos".

questions.question: What do children in many countries hunt for at Easter?
questions.fact: The Easter Bunny tradition came from Germany, where a hare was said to bring eggs to good children.

questions.question: Which pastry is eaten at China's Mid-Autumn Festival?
questions.fact: Mooncakes are round like the full moon, and often have a salted egg yolk hidden inside.

questions.question: What does the Japanese tradition of "hanami" celebrate?
questions.fact: During hanami, people have picnics under the blossoming cherry trees. The blossoms last only about a week or two.

questions.question: Which country celebrates Midsummer with a maypole and dancing in June?
questions.fact: Swedes celebrate Midsummer with pickled herring, new potatoes, strawberries, and songs like "Små grodorna".

questions.question: Oktoberfest takes place in which city?
questions.fact: Oktoberfest began in 1810 to celebrate a royal wedding in Munich.

questions.question: Despite its name, Oktoberfest mostly takes place in…
questions.fact: Oktoberfest was moved earlier into September for warmer weather. It ends on the first weekend of October.

questions.question: What is traditionally eaten at Thanksgiving dinner in the USA?
questions.fact: Around 46 million turkeys are eaten in the USA each Thanksgiving, and the President "pardons" one every year.

questions.question: Bastille Day is the national day of which country?
questions.fact: Bastille Day celebrates the storming of the Bastille prison in 1789, the start of the French Revolution.

questions.question: On what date is Bastille Day?
questions.fact: A big military parade goes down the Champs-Élysées in Paris every 14 July.

questions.question: On what date is Independence Day in the USA?
questions.fact: The Declaration of Independence was approved on 4 July 1776.

questions.question: On what date is Spain's National Day?
questions.fact: 12 October marks the day in 1492 when Columbus reached the Americas. It's also the feast day of the Virgen del Pilar.

questions.question: Which Spanish holiday falls on 6 December?
questions.fact: Spain's Constitution was approved by a referendum on 6 December 1978.

questions.question: Saint Patrick's Day is the national day of…
questions.fact: Saint Patrick is said to have used the three-leafed shamrock to explain the Holy Trinity.

questions.question: Which colour do people wear on Saint Patrick's Day?
questions.fact: Saint Patrick was originally linked to the colour blue. Green came later, for Ireland's nickname "the Emerald Isle".

questions.question: Who is celebrated on Burns Night in Scotland?
questions.fact: On Burns Night (25 January), Scots eat haggis and read Burns's poem "Address to a Haggis". He also wrote "Auld Lang Syne".

questions.question: How is Guy Fawkes Night (5 November) celebrated in the UK?
questions.fact: It remembers the failed 1605 plot to blow up the English Parliament. People burn "Guy" dummies on bonfires.

questions.question: What is Boxing Day?
questions.fact: The name is often linked to the boxes of gifts or money once given to servants and workers on that day.

questions.question: Which city is famous for the world's biggest Carnival parade with samba schools?
questions.fact: Rio's Carnival parade is held in the Sambadrome, a stadium built just for the samba schools.

questions.question: The Carnival of Venice is famous for its…
questions.fact: Venetian masks let people of all classes mix freely without being recognised.

questions.question: Which Spanish city's Carnival is famous for funny satirical songs called "chirigotas"?
questions.fact: Cádiz's Carnival groups spend all year writing their funny songs and compete in the Gran Teatro Falla.

questions.question: What is the Jewish New Year called?
questions.fact: On Rosh Hashanah, people dip apples in honey to wish for a sweet new year.

questions.question: Eid al-Fitr marks the end of…
questions.fact: Eid al-Fitr celebrations often start with special prayers and a big family meal with sweets.

questions.question: About how many days does Lent last?
questions.fact: Lent's 40 days remember Jesus's 40 days in the desert. Sundays traditionally aren't counted.

questions.question: What is the day before Lent, famous for pancakes in the UK?
questions.fact: Shrove Tuesday is Carnival or "Mardi Gras", meaning "Fat Tuesday", in other countries: a last feast before Lent.

questions.question: What is the calendar with little doors you open before Christmas called?
questions.fact: The first printed Advent calendars appeared in Germany in the early 1900s. Chocolate ones came later.

questions.question: How many candles are usually on an Advent wreath?
questions.fact: Some Advent wreaths have a fifth white candle in the middle, lit on Christmas Day.

questions.question: In which country is it a tradition to eat KFC at Christmas?
questions.fact: A 1970s KFC advertising campaign in Japan made a "Christmas bucket" so popular that people order weeks ahead.

questions.question: In the Philippines, when does the Christmas season famously start?
questions.fact: In the Philippines, Christmas songs start playing in the "ber" months, from September onwards.

questions.question: Which country calls its New Year's Eve celebration "Hogmanay"?
questions.fact: A Hogmanay tradition is "first-footing": the first visitor after midnight brings gifts for luck.

questions.question: In which country do people jump off chairs at midnight on New Year's Eve?
questions.fact: Danes also smash old plates on friends' doors on New Year's Eve. A big pile means lots of friends!

questions.question: What colour of underwear is worn for luck on New Year's Eve in Spain and Italy?
questions.fact: Red underwear on New Year's Eve is said to bring luck in love. Some say it works best if someone gives it to you.

questions.question: In which country do thousands of sky lanterns float up during the Yi Peng festival?
questions.fact: Yi Peng lanterns carry wishes up into the sky, and the festival happens around November's full moon.

questions.question: What do people do during Songkran, the Thai New Year?
questions.fact: Songkran happens in mid-April, the hottest time of year in Thailand. The water stands for washing away bad luck.

questions.question: What is a piñata usually filled with?
questions.fact: Piñatas are hugely popular in Mexico, especially at birthdays and Christmas "posadas".

questions.question: Which Dutch holiday on 27 April has everyone wearing orange?
questions.fact: King's Day celebrates King Willem-Alexander's birthday. Orange is the colour of the Dutch royal family, the House of Orange.

questions.question: What do children in the UK and US leave out for Santa?
questions.fact: Children often leave a carrot for the reindeer too. In the UK, Santa sometimes gets a mince pie and a glass of sherry.

questions.question: What do Spanish children leave out for the Three Kings' camels?
questions.fact: Spanish children also leave their shoes out for the Kings, who leave gifts or a lump of sweet "coal" for naughty kids.

questions.question: What is "Nochevieja"?
questions.fact: On Nochevieja, Spaniards eat 12 grapes at midnight, one for each chime of the clock.

questions.question: What is "Nochebuena"?
questions.fact: On Nochebuena, Spanish families usually have a big dinner together. Some go to "Misa del Gallo", Midnight Mass.
